name: University of Suffolk

settingEvidence.evidence: The University’s main campus is located on the stunning Ipswich Waterfront. ... it is also just a short walk away from the town centre

fees.text: £10,050 per year for UK full-time students starting in 2027 (2027/28), as shown on the course pages. Suffolk reserves the right to change fees in line with legislation or government decisions. Its general UK fees page still quotes £9,790 per year (no year given).

source.evidence: 2027/28 UK Full-time Tuition Fee £10,050* per year

livingCosts.text: Halls and the off-campus houses Suffolk recommends cost about £139-£215 a week including bills and Wi-Fi, self-catered (2026/27 prices, correct as of March 2026). Athena Hall, on campus, is £139-£215 a week depending on room type and tenancy length (44 or 51 weeks).

source.evidence: Prices shown are for the 2026–2027 academic year, correct as of March 2026. ... All room prices include utility bills and Wi-Fi ... £139 ... £215

openDays.text: Next open day: Saturday 14 November 2026, 9.30am-2.00pm at the Ipswich campus. Later dates are not announced yet. Suffolk offers up to £50 towards travel if your round trip is 100 miles or more.

contextual.summary: If you live in a lower-participation area, have a declared disability, have lived in local authority care or are a young carer aged 25 or under, you are automatically considered for a contextual offer.
contextual.typicalReduction: Normally at least one grade lower than the published entry requirement (e.g. 112 tariff points, BBC, becomes 104 points, BCC), or an unconditional offer.

criteria.detail: Living in an area classed as Quintile 1 or 2 in the Index of Multiple Deprivation (IMD).
Living in an area classed as Quintile 1 or 2 in the POLAR4 Index.
Has lived in Local Authority Care.
Has a caring responsibility (confirmed on UCAS) and is aged 25 or under at the point of application.

contextual.rulesText: Applicants who meet one or more of the criteria are automatically considered for a contextual offer: an unconditional offer, or a conditional offer on a lower tariff than the published entry requirements. Interviews, references, placement experience, Occupational Health or DBS requirements still apply where a course needs them. Suffolk also signs Progression Agreements with some schools and colleges to make lower conditional offers to students in those schools.

source.evidence: Applicants who meet one of more of the following criteria will be automatically considered for a contextual offer:

programmes.summary: A summer school for Year 12 (or equivalent) students with university-style subject tasters, preparing-for-university workshops, and team-building and social activities.

notes: Suffolk does not offer an Economics degree: its course finder (checked 2026-10-21) returns no undergraduate Economics, Politics, PPE or Real Estate course. The closest matches are BA (Hons) Business Management and BSc (Hons) Accounting and Finance, both taught in Ipswich. The 'economics' link points to the Business and Accounting subject page.
No 2028-entry pages yet: both course pages show year of entry 2027/28 (September 2027 start), so 2027 entry is recorded.
Offers are given in UCAS tariff points (112 points = BBC at A level). No admissions test is listed, and Suffolk is not on UAT-UK's official TMUA list for 2027 entry.

Not recorded: BA (Hons) Business Management (Top-Up, N207) is for people with an HND or FdA; BA (Hons) Leadership and Management (N202) is taught at East Coast College in Great Yarmouth, not in Ipswich.

Entry rules page: at least two A-level subjects (or equivalent) are usually required, applicants are expected to hold three GCSEs at grade C/4 or above, and the Admissions Tutor may ask an applicant to attend an interview.
Athena Hall is the on-campus halls; the accommodation price table also lists accredited off-campus houses Suffolk recommends (75 Grimwade Street, Ormonde House). All rooms are self-catered.
Suffolk offers up to £50 towards the cost of visiting an open day if your round trip is 100 miles or more, or if you meet its widening participation criteria.
